summary: Hisao Takahashi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1972–1977) and under Ryukai Mano. He held various positions at Taisho University (~1977–2015, including professor) and worked at the Institute for Contemporary Edification, Shingon-shu Buzan-ha.

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and as an associate professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato (1913–2008) was a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He later served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Komazawa University, and Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1977–1984).

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, also studying under Akira Saitō, Hiroshi Marui, Yoichi Fukuda, and Masahiro Inami, and became a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University.

Hisatake Kato (1937–2020) was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, Yamagata University, Tohoku University, Tottori University of Environmental Studies, and the University of Human Arts and Sciences.

Hisayoshi Miyamoto is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. Formerly a professor at Toyo University, his positions attested in 2026 include lectureships at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He has held positions at Koyasan University (attested 1986, and as professor in 2015) and at the Institute of Esoteric Buddhist Culture (attested 1992).

Hitoshi Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He held appointments at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Otani University (all attested 1992), and served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017).

Hla Pe (1913–2007) was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon, the UCL Institute of Education, and SOAS University of London. He spent his career at SOAS teaching Burmese language and culture, serving as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Yang completed a PhD at the University of Washington (ending 1994) under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.
Hoin Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1959–1963) and studied under Gyoin Hashimoto as a disciple.
Hoju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University (~1999–2003) and KU Leuven (~2005–2007), and taught Kyokuga Saeki.

Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar. Affiliations attested in 2026 include Minobusan University (assistant professor and assistant director), the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and part-time lectureships at Doho University and the Daido University graduate school.

Hojun Nagasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He served at Otani University (~1968–1999) and became president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies in 1998.
Hokei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and later served there as a professor from around 1921 to 1944.
Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and holds a director post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009). She joined the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

Holmes Welch (1924–1981) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earning degrees at Harvard University (~1940–1957). He taught as a lecturer at Harvard and Yale, and served as assistant director of the Center for the Study of World Religions (~1964–1968).

Hong Luo specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, having studied as a doctoral student at Peking University. Luo has held positions at the China Tibetology Research Center, Sichuan University as a professor, and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Hongyue Guo is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo earned a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and also studied under Xubang Qi.
